name: React + FastAPI + PostgreSQL
description: A second web golden stack: a React (Vite) single-page frontend served by a FastAPI backend, talking to PostgreSQL through SQLAlchemy/Alembic — materially different from nextjs-postgres (separate frontend/backend languages and frameworks, a real Alembic downgrade instead of a hand-written rollback script).

inputs.name: projectName
inputs.description: Package name used for both the frontend and backend manifests of the generated app.

inputs.name: includeAuth
inputs.description: Scaffold a starter session-cookie auth module.

inputs.name: orm
inputs.description: ORM used to talk to PostgreSQL.

generatedArtifacts.description: FastAPI backend manifest with pinned dependency ranges.
SQLAlchemy models — the single source of truth for the data model.
React/Vite frontend manifest with pinned dependency ranges.
Multi-stage production build (frontend build stage -> Python runtime) used for the deployment-package control.

verification.command: cd backend && mypy app && cd ../frontend && npm run typecheck
verification.description: Backend strict mypy and frontend TypeScript both compile with no errors.

verification.command: cd backend && pytest && cd ../tests/e2e && npm test
verification.description: Backend unit/integration suite and frontend e2e suite both pass.
Production multi-stage build succeeds, proving the build control.

operationalEvidence.evidence: Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/ give a repeatable, versioned persistence lifecycle.
Alembic supports a real downgrade() natively; the generated migration ships forward and backward paths together, rehearsed end to end.
The generated multi-stage Dockerfile builds a pinned, reproducible production image that serves the built frontend directly from FastAPI.
